title: Communication Quality and the Cost of Language: Evidence from Stack Overflow
eligible_reason: Staggered introduction of four non-English Stack Overflow sites (Russian 2010, Portuguese 2013, Japanese 2014, Spanish 2015) treats non-native-English answerers at four distinct dates, with a never-treated random sample of English-only users as controls. Table 3 reports, for two outcomes (numCodes, isBestAnswer), a no-controls TWFE column (xtreg Y after i.weekdate, fe; user FE + week FE) and a no-controls Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation column (did_imputation Y user weekdate event_week). Binary absorbing treatment, unit and calendar-time FE, no controls: eligible. The remaining Table 3 columns add answer-level time-varying controls and are not eligible.
design_notes: Answer-level data (323,850 answers, 5,339 users, 472 weeks Jul 2008 - Aug 2017), repeated cross-section assigned to users: unit = user (xtset user), calendar time = weekdate; several answers per user-week (mean 3.7). Treated group = users active in both English and another language (286,801 answers); control = random sample of English-only users (37,049 answers, TreatmentGroup == 'Control'). Cohort variable 'cohort' takes 5 values (4 language cohorts + control) and is the cluster variable in all Table 3 regressions. after agrees with (weekdate >= event_week) for 99.94% of treated rows (small timing discrepancy, event_day based); use the authors' after for TWFE and event_week for BJS/CSA. Table 3 columns TWFE 1-3 / BJS 1-3 add question_numcodes, question_answer_count, question_view_count (time-varying answer-level controls) and TWFE 3 / BJS 3 add same_language and picture_empathy FE: not eligible. Tables 4-5: after x question-quality / incentive category interactions (subgroup-by-treatment): not eligible. Appendix EC tables repeat the design on subsamples (not main text). Section 8 analyses (UsersNoEng_Posts.dta, new vs old joiners) are not DiD.
n_eligible_specs_note: 2 TWFE specs (numCodes, isBestAnswer) plus their 2 reported BJS counterparts; the TWFE/BJS pair for one outcome is one design.
never_treated_note: TreatmentGroup == 'Control': 37,049 answers from English-only users (random sample), event_week missing.
always_treated_note: Russian cohort treated 2010-10-08; sample starts 2008-07-29, so all cohorts have pre-periods (verify per user).
preferred_spec_note: unclear without article text; numCodes is the primary quality measure (Table 3 first panel), isBestAnswer the secondary one.

published_estimates.source: authors' replication output Outputs/Correct.tex col (1) 'TWFE'; Table 3 in the paper is a manual merge of Correct.tex and CorrectBestAnswer.tex, so published column numbers may differ

data_access_note: Stack Exchange data dump (archive.org) processed by the author; final estimation dataset shipped.
data_files: Data/finJRSP_estimationdata_torun_NEWVER.dta (323,850 rows x 86 vars; Table 3-5 and EC tables)
software: stata (regressions; did_imputation, reghdfe, estout); python (figures, descriptives)
screener_notes: Clean staggered design with 4 cohorts and never-treated controls; author already reports BJS next to TWFE (BJS roughly 1.5x TWFE for numCodes, 4.7x for isBestAnswer). Key implementation details: unit = user, time = week, observation = answer (unbalanced, repeated cross-section within user-week); authors cluster on 5 cohorts, which will fail the protocol's leverage screen, so record a deviation (e.g., cluster by user) if needed. Published Table 3 is a manual merge of two output tables; confirm column mapping and the exact published coefficients against the article PDF when available.
